chunk_findings.detail: `GitProbes.__init__` defaults `min_git` to `"2.38"`, but this change exists so conflict detection uses the probe's 2.43 `merge-tree` gate and scratch-merge fallback (the new module docstring says an older git must not come back as "could not tell" for a version reason). Any still-valid one-arg call `GitProbes(repo)` — the previous signature — forwards `min_git="2.38"`. On git 2.40, `probe.run` then treats `--write-tree` as allowed, hits the pre-2.43 exit-code bug, and returns unavailable, so `conflicts` yields `None` instead of the scratch-merge bool. Only `api/metrics.py` passes `cfg.locks.probe_merge_tree_min_git`; the class default reintroduces the drift the wrapper was meant to remove. The new test always constructs `GitProbes(..., min_git="2.43")` and stubs `probe_run`, so it never sees this input.

chunk_findings.detail: `p = GitProbes(tmp_path, 30, "2.38")` explicitly sets `min_git` back to the old unsafe threshold. `probe.run` treats `min_git="2.38"` as permission to use `git merge-tree --write-tree` on Git 2.38 and later, but versions 2.38–2.42 have the pre-2.43 exit-code defect the probe’s new threshold exists to avoid; on those versions the probe returns `UNAVAILABLE`, so `p.conflicts(main, side) is True` and `p.conflicts(base, side) is False` in this same test receive `None` and fail. The safe default/omitted `min_git` would route Git 2.38–2.42 through the scratch-merge fallback instead, so this changed line should not force `"2.38"`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lock_metrics.py:202

chunk_findings.detail: The only real-git check of `GitProbes.conflicts` was updated to `GitProbes(tmp_path, 30, "2.38")` and then asserts `p.conflicts(main, side) is True` on branches that actually conflict. `min_git="2.38"` is the gate this change was written to stop using: on git 2.40 (at least 2.38, before 2.43) `probe.run` treats `merge-tree --write-tree` as allowed, hits the pre-2.43 exit-code bug, and returns unavailable, so `conflicts` returns `None` and the assertion fails (or, if that bug reports exit 0, returns `False` for a real conflict). The new module docstring promises an older git falls back to a scratch merge and is never "could not tell" for a version reason; this call opts the regression guard back into the broken threshold instead of `probe_merge_tree_min_git` / `"2.43"`.

chunk_findings.detail: `module_names` never refuses a duplicated module name, so the advertised multi-path scan can hide a section instead of raising. `pkgutil.iter_modules` walks every entry of `package.__path__` and the comprehension only sorts; given `__path__ == [dir_a, dir_b]` where both contain `agent.py`, it returns `("agent", "agent", ...)`. `SECTION_MODULES` then calls `import_module` twice, the second hit is the `sys.modules` cache, and the other file never runs, so `@declare` never sees the clash. chunk_findings.detail: The test `test_a_new_section_module_is_discovered_without_editing_shared_files` monkeypatches `ddflow.config_sections.__path__` *after* `ddflow.config` and `ddflow.config_sections` have already been imported and their module-level execution has run. At that point, `SECTION_NAMES` and `SECTION_MODULES` in `ddflow.config_sections` have already been evaluated and will not contain `zzz_throwaway`. Therefore, when the test asserts `"zzz_throwaway" in CS.module_names(CS)`, `CS.module_names(CS)` scans `CS`, whose `__path__` is still the original package directory (not `tmp_path / "extra_sections"`), so `"zzz_throwaway"` is never in `CS.module_names(CS)` and the test fails or produces a false outcome (or `importlib.import_module` succeeds only because it imports an arbitrary path that was never integrated into the package's `SECTION_NAMES` or `SECTION_MODULES`).

chunk_findings.detail: The test `test_a_new_section_wires_into_a_fresh_config_process` runs a subprocess that mutates `CS.__path__` *after* importing `ddflow.config_sections`, but it never imports or executes the discovery scanner *after* appending to `__path__`. `SECTION_NAMES` and `SECTION_MODULES` in `ddflow.config_sections` are evaluated at import time of `ddflow.config_sections` (when `__path__` only contained the original package directory). Consequently, the new throwaway section file is never loaded into `SECTION_MODULES`, causing the subprocess execution to fail or test nothing of the actual startup discovery integration because `importlib.import_module('ddflow.config_sections.zzz_throwaway')` is called directly rather than being discovered via the scan during `import ddflow.config`.

chunk_findings.detail: In `ddflow/config_sections/__init__.py`, `SECTION_MODULES` is evaluated at import time: `SECTION_MODULES = tuple(importlib.import_module(f"{__name__}.{n}") for n in SECTION_NAMES)`. Because `SECTION_NAMES` is derived from `module_names(sys.modules[__name__])` which uses `__path__` at import time, if tests modify `ddflow.config_sections.__path__` dynamically (as seen in `test_a_new_section_module_is_discovered_without_editing_shared_files`), `SECTION_MODULES` and `SECTION_NAMES` do not automatically pick up newly added path entries unless re-imported or re-evaluated, which can lead to stale registries if a caller inspects `SECTION_MODULES` after modifying `__path__`.
